messages.subject: Problem with oSCR
parts:
Hi oSCR group,


I have tested some models with my white-tailed deer encounter history data. Everything goes otherwise smoothly and the resulting coefficients are logical, but the density map doesn’t seem to be correct. predict.oSCR predicts the distribution of animals to be in illogical places i.e. around traps where there are no recaptures. First I thought there might be something wrong in the coordinates but the coordinate file seems to be correct. There might be some obvious mistake in the code, which I can’t see.


I attached my edf and tdf files here and also the code.

I would appreciate if you could take a look at them if you have any corrections or comments.


Code:


#data2oscr

data <- data2oscr(edf, sess.col=1, id.col=2, occ.col = 3, trap.col = 4, sex.col = 5, tdf = list(tdf), K = c(2), ntraps = c(116), remove.zeros = TRUE, remove.extracaps = TRUE)

 

# Make the SCRframe

scrFrame  <- make.scrFrame(caphist=data$y3d,  traps=data$traplocs, indCovs = data$sex, trapCovs=NULL , trapOperation=data$trapopp )

 

# Make a state-space object

ssDF <-make.ssDF(scrFrame, buffer=600, res=200)

 

#plot SSDF and trap points

plot(ssDF)

points(scrFrame$traps[[1]],pch=19, lwd=0.5,col="red")

 

#basic SCR null model, constant density, p0 and sigma

m0 <- oSCR.fit(model=list(D~1,p0~1,sig~1), scrFrame=scrFrame, ssDF=ssDF,plotit=FALSE )

#occassion specif p0

mT <- oSCR.fit(model=list(D~1,p0~t,sig~1), scrFrame=scrFrame, ssDF=ssDF,plotit=FALSE )

 

#model selection

fl <- fitList.oSCR(list(m0,mT),

                   rename=T)

ms <- modSel.oSCR(fl)

 

#AIC table

ms$aic.tab

#coeficient tabel

ms$coef.tab


# Make a prediction object from the model
#Produces data objects necessary to create a map
#of realized density and posterior distributions
#of activity centers.

pred<- predict.oSCR(scrFrame,mT ,ssDF)


# Plot total density map

par(mfrow=c(1,1))

plot(pred$r[[1]])

points(tdf[,2:3],pch=20, lwd=0.5)

title("Density")

 

#check that the trap coordinates are correct and trap IDs correspond the location

plot(tdf$X,tdf$Y,pch=19,type='n')

text(tdf$X,tdf$Y,as.character(tdf$ID))

 

 

Thanks,

Jenni Poutanen

PhD student

Department of Biology

University of Turku, Finland

Hi Jenni, and everyone,

 

It seems as though data2oscr() function was creating the capture histories incorrectly, specifically attributing captures to the wrong traps.

I will need to figure out exactly why that happens, and why it hasn’t been picked up before.

 

Here is the code I used to recreate the analysis that that Jon had done. It requires the latest version which you can access like this:

 

devtools::install_github("jaroyle/oSCR")

And then here is the script:

edf$TrapID <- factor(edf$TrapID,levels=unique(tdf$ID))

edf$Occasion <- factor(edf$Occasion,levels=1:2)

edf$ID <- factor(edf$ID,levels=unique(edf$ID))

 

tdf$TrapID <- factor(tdf$ID)

 

tmp.y <- with(edf, tapply(ID,list(ID,TrapID,Occasion),length))

tmp.y[is.na(tmp.y)] <- 0

tmp.y <- ifelse(tmp.y>0,1,0)

tmp.sex <- tapply(edf$Sex,edf$ID,unique)-1

 

scrFrame <- make.scrFrame(caphist = list(tmp.y),

                          traps = list(tdf[,c("X","Y")]),

                          indCovs = list(data.frame(sex=tmp.sex)))

ssDF <-make.ssDF(scrFrame, buffer=600, res=100)

plot(ssDF, scrFrame)

m0 <- oSCR.fit(model=list(D~1,p0~1,sig~1), scrFrame=scrFrame, ssDF=ssDF)

pred<- predict.oSCR(scrFrame,mT ,ssDF)

plot(pred$r[[1]])

andy

Hi Jenni,

Can you paste the oSCR output table from the full model?

Similar to other R models, covariates in oSCR are estimated with an effects parameterization on the link scale.  In fact, all parameter results in oSCR are reported on the link scale.  To get values on the real scale (e.g. probabilities, etc.) you need to back-transform, being sure to add the intercept to effect estimates where relevant.

For example, probability of capture for females and males would be:

plogis("p0.(Intercept)")                       #females
plogis("p0.(Intercept)" + "p0.males")  #males

This is why you have psi values that are >1, those values are on the logit scale.

The estimates from the sex specific sigma model are for the linear predictor. So, for example, if the male sigma was double that of females, then the female sigma and the male EFFECT would be similar, so when you exponentiate the parameters they are similar. But, what you should do is add the male effect to the intercept (female).

 

So for the sex specific siga model:

 

female sigma = exp( intercept )

male sigma = exp( intercept + male )

 

Also note that the ‘t*sex’ detection model is exactly the same as the ‘t+sex’ model. That’s because this is a very unstable model and we didn’t implement it I think. I thought I had a warning in there to that effect.

Hi Jenni,

Sorry, I was asking for the printed output for a single model (e.g.,mTS4).  The "outStats" object of a fitted model will tell you the link scales for each of the parameters.  Density and sigma are always log scale, while p0 can be either logit or log scale, depending on the encounter model chosen (by default it is logit with a Binomial encounter model).  The psi sex ratio is always logit scale.

Given the effects parameterization, you always need to include the intercept and then any relevant effects in the linear predictor for a given group before back-transforming.  In your case:

p0.t1.male = plogis(p0.intercept + p.males)

p0.t2.male = plogis(p0.intercept + p.t2 + p.males)

The estimates from the sex specific sigma model are for the linear predictor. So, for example, if the male sigma was double that of females, then the female sigma and the male EFFECT would be similar, so when you exponentiate the parameters they are similar. But, what you should do is add the male effect to the intercept (female).

 

So for the sex specific siga model:

 

female sigma = exp( intercept )

male sigma = exp( intercept + male )

 

Also note that the ‘t*sex’ detection model is exactly the same as the ‘t+sex’ model. That’s because this is a very unstable model and we didn’t implement it I think. I thought I had a warning in there to that effect.
